summary:
Thought I’d write a second letter to cover a greater span of my life, over these many years. I believe when I wrote you I was married to a woman named Anne who had three children from a previous marriage and who lived out in the rural part of West Marin. We were married seven years and had one child, Laura, who still writes me—in fact Laura is the only one, child or ex-wife, who writes me. I had to commit Anne to a mental hospital, and soon after, our mar­ riage broke up. I escaped to Oakland, where I met a girl named Nancy, who was just recovering from a schizophrenic attack and hospitalization, so you can see at 
a glance I was following a pattern in my marriages. Nancy and I had one child, too, a girl, Isolde (I may have written you about that.) I labored to build up a home for my family: all the modem appliances, plus a four-bedroom, two-bathroom tract type house. Things seemed to be going fine, but then Nancy became mentally ill again, and I had to commit her to a psychiatric hospital. When she came out she stayed only two weeks and then ran off with the man across the street, who was also married and had a little girl. Suddenly there I was, alone, in the four-bedroom house with all the appliances, but no wife and no little girl. The history of my life was repeating itself, frighteningly. I tried to commit sui­ cide, but the Crisis Center (the Help Line) intervened and got my head together. That was in August 1970. I brought all sorts of people into the house to give it ...
